subject: Re: Intermittent fragment drops on private link after cutover
messages:
From: Alex Palmer <alex.palmer@equinox.com>

Cc: Equinox Network Ops <netops@equinox.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent fragment drops on private link after cutover

Hi Ben,

We cut over our private connector to Redwood's VPC this morning (per the cutover playbook). Since about 07:50 PDT we're seeing intermittent packet drops between our on-prem collector (10.2.5.12) and a handful of internal services running in the private VPC. Symptoms:

- UDP/collector traffic shows ~15-25% packet loss post-cutover (no packet loss pre-cutover).
- Wireshark traces show repeated IP fragments and a number of reassembly failures on the on-prem side.
- When we bypass the transit box and point traffic directly to the gateway the loss goes away.

We've attached a short pcap from the collector (equinox_cutover_capture.pcap) and a routing dump from the transit device (private-link-routing.txt). We suspect an MTU/fragmentation path issue or an intermediate NAT device dropping fragments during hairpin flows.

This is impacting telemetry and export pipelines. Can your network team triage? We can be on a call — available between 09:00-11:30 PDT.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Palmer
NetOps Lead, Equinox Inc.
Mobile: +1 415 555 0132

Subject: Re: Intermittent fragment drops on private link after cutover

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and the captures, appreciate the timestamps. Looping in our network engineering and account owner to coordinate.

Initial asks so we can triage quickly:
- Can you confirm the MTU configured on the transit box and on the on-prem collector interface?
- Do you have the NAT translation table for the transit device (if hairpin NAT is in use)?
- Any recent firewall/SG rules applied as part of the cutover?

Karthik/Naomi — taking on the investigation. Based on Alex's note my working hypothesis is: 1) PMTU mismatch (or missing MSS clamp) causing IP fragmentation, 2) an intermediate device (transit NAT box) is not handling fragments or is dropping non-first fragments, or 3) asymmetric routing causing reassembly to fail at the wrong hop.

Immediate suggestion for customer (we can run with this if you confirm): enable MSS clamping on the transit device for TCP (to prevent fragmentation) and temporarily add a /32 host route that pins return path to the VPC gateway for the collector IP to avoid hairpin/translation.

We'll open an internal incident (JIRA-OPS-1287) and schedule a triage call at 09:15 PDT unless you prefer earlier.

Subject: Re: Intermittent fragment drops on private link after cutover

Ben / team — quick triage notes from my side after looking at the pcap and routing dump Alex sent:

- Observed behavior: sequences of IP fragments where the initial fragment (offset 0) is forwarded but later fragments are not reaching the on-prem reassembly engine. Several packets show DF=0 and fragmentation offsets present.
- Routing: the transit device shows a policy-based NAT for traffic originating from the VPC to the collector that will hairpin back through the same device. That aligns with the cutover config.
- Security groups: I noticed SGs on the VPC side allow the flows but the transit filter has explicit fragment handling disabled (i.e., drop fragments unless they match a stateful session).

Immediate checks for Equinox to run (can run quickly):
1) On the transit box: show ip nat translations | include 10.2.5.12 and ip route get 10.2.5.12 from <vpc-gateway-ip>
2) On the on-prem collector host: sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 "ip[6:2] & 0x1fff != 0" -w fragments.pcap (captures only non-zero-fragment packets)
3) If transit device supports it, enable MSS clamping for TCP (example for a linux-based router):
   iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
   (I put a small script mss-clamp-suggest.sh in attachments that mirror this)

Workaround plan:
- Apply MSS clamp on transit for a 1-hour trial and monitor. This avoids fragmentation for TCP; for UDP we need to ensure PMTU is enforced or route-level MTU is consistent.
- Add a transient /32 route (or policy route) on the transit box that pins return path for 10.2.5.12 to the VPC gateway to avoid NAT hairpin for the collector flows.

Longer term: standardize PMTU checks in the cutover runbook and enforce an MTU verification step with a small UDP probe. Also remove any transit filters that drop fragments unless strictly required.

I can jump on the call at 09:15.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 12:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent fragment drops on private link after cutover — remediation and follow-up

Alex — quick update and what we changed during the 09:15 triage call:

What we did (validated):
- Enabled MSS clamping on the transit device for forwarded TCP flows (rolled back after test showed improvement to confirm).
- Added a temporary host route on the transit box to pin return traffic for 10.2.5.12 via the VPC gateway (avoids hairpin NAT for collector packets).
- Temporarily relaxed fragment filtering on the transit filter to allow non-initial fragments while we confirm reassembly at the on-prem collector.

Outcome:
- Collector telemetry returned to normal (loss dropped from ~18% to <1%). Wireshark traces show reassembly success for prior fragmented flows.

Next steps / remediation plan:
1) We'll leave the host route in place for 24 hours while monitoring. If stable, we'll convert to a policy route in the transit policy to be persistent.
2) We'll add a PMTU verification step to the private cutover checklist and an explicit MSS-clamp guardrail for transit devices that do not do automatic PMTU discovery.
3) Action item for Redwood Engineering: remove strict fragment-drop filters from transit or provide an explicit exception for known private-connector flows (JIRA-OPS-1287).

Can we schedule a 30-minute postmortem tomorrow at 10:00 PDT to review the cutover checklist and sign off on the policy changes? I added the drive doc with the remediation notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/eqx/private-cutover-notes

Thanks for the patience and quick validation on your side — glad we got the collector stable.

Best,
Ben Carter
